title: fix: make a failed generation visible instead of silently resetting
body:
Follow-up to #958. Three fixes, all about a generation failing without telling anyone.

## 1. A failed tailored generation silently reset to the wizard

`TailorFlow` derives its stage as `generating → done if there is output → else configuring`. A failed run leaves both outputs empty, so it fell back to the wizard — and the file contained **zero references to `error`**. `runTailor` wrote the message to the session, the hook returned it, nothing rendered it, and the catch only `console.error`d, so there was no toast either. The result was a generation that appeared to do nothing at all, which cost two investigations to reproduce.

Returning to the wizard is right — the user needs to change something and retry — but it has to arrive with the reason. The error now renders below the wizard where the user just clicked Generate, and a toast fires, matching what the AI Generate wizard already did. The toast carries a fixed translated string; the raw provider message goes in the panel, not a transient toast.

The test drives a real failure through the hook and asserts the rendered text rather than the store field — a test that only checked the field was set would have passed against the broken code, which is how this survived.

## 2. The stream deadline was not scaled by reasoning effort

300 s, hardcoded on both the Rust and renderer sides. `reqwest`'s `RequestBuilder::timeout` bounds the **whole** request — connect through the last streamed byte — so a generation that legitimately runs longer is killed mid-stream. High effort on a large cloud model with a full résumé plus job ad sits squarely in that range, and is the likely throw behind the failure in §1.

Both sides now scale by the request's effort, with the renderer as the outer bound so the backend's actionable provider error fires first rather than a generic renderer timeout. The tables can't be shared across the IPC boundary, so a test hardcodes the backend schedule and asserts the renderer exceeds it at every tier.

**Worth flagging:** the tier order is the vendors' — `max` sits **above** `xhigh` (Anthropic's effort docs, OpenAI's `reasoning_effort`). That reads wrong at a glance and was inverted in the first cut, giving the highest-effort runs the *shortest* deadline. Both monotonicity tests listed the tiers in that same wrong order, so they passed against it; only the value assertions caught it. Both tables and both arrays now carry a comment saying why the order is what it is.

Rejected alternative: a per-chunk idle timeout would be architecturally nicer, but it would mean loosening the total timeout at all four call sites plus a second timing mechanism inside the shared stream loop — and it wouldn't need effort-awareness at all. Documented in `timeouts.rs`.

## 3. A truncated generation was saved as complete

`finish()` consulted `stop_reason` only inside the `is_empty` branch, so a stream that emitted text and then reported `finish_reason: "length"` took the success path: terminal event, `job_complete`, persisted result. A truncated résumé or cover letter was saved and exported as if finished. `parse_openai_finish_reason` already produced `StopReason::Length`; it was simply unused on the non-empty path.

It still completes and still keeps the partial text — that text is worth having, and this must not be fatal — but it now raises a notification through the existing Notification Center (the same seam `email_watch_scheduler` and `reminder_scheduler` use) rather than presenting a cut-off document as done.

## 4. Carried over from #958

`gemini_is_recognized_pre_v3` additionally required a `gemini-` prefix, so a `gemma-*` or `learnlm-*` id — which Google's listing surfaces, since `parse_model_page` filters on `models/` and not on family — got a fully neutral profile while every other gate in that file keys only on the v3 boundary. The gate is now the exact inversion of the v3 check. Confirmed while there that the v3 check cannot misclassify a Gemma id: it requires the literal prefix before parsing any version digits.

## Testing

`cargo test --all-features` (incl. architecture) · renderer suite · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` · `cargo fmt`.

Note: this was pushed with `--no-verify` at the author's request, so the pre-push gate did not run. The full `pnpm test` / `typecheck` / `lint:strict` sweep is CI's here rather than local.

title: fix: stop the resume prompt licensing invented metrics, and let each provider own its sampling
body:
Two related changes to generation quality, folded together because the second depends on the first.

## 1. Prompt contradictions

Prompt sizes were **measured** with a real tokenizer before anything was touched — résumé 4,563 tokens, analyze 5,684, cover letter 4,058. Size was never the problem and nothing was rewritten for it. `locale/index.ts` is 973 lines and contributes 40 tokens per request; `links.ts` is 1,221 lines and contributes 0. The defect was contradiction density in the `full` tier of two files.

**The résumé prompt licensed inventing metrics.** It said *"NEVER fabricate numbers - only use metrics if they're in the original **or can be reasonably inferred**"*, two lines after mandating that every bullet carry a measurable result, with ATS mode adding "quantify every achievement" — while three other rules in the same prompt banned exactly what that clause permits. The `brief` tier and the Rust port of the same spine both got it right, so the `full` tier, the one cloud users hit, was the outlier. A résumé with an invented number is one the candidate has to defend in an interview.

**The analyze prompt fought itself over keyword matching.** *"Synonyms fail 70% of the time"* and *"Hard Skills: Must match EXACTLY"*, then 150 lines later *"React.js = React = ReactJS"* — while the user prompt and the Rust `SYNONYMS` map both implement semantic matching. That decides `missingKeywords` and `keywordCoverage`, which the user sees. The ATS score was also decomposed two incompatible ways in one system prompt.

Also removed: ~500 tokens instructing a weighted `overall` score that has no field in the schema (only `overallAssessment: string`), a `### CANDIDATE RESUME ###` header emitted ~170 lines after the résumé it announces, a leaked `topRequirements` variable name, and a duplicate point budget. The German subject label now goes through the output-language fitter like the salutation and sign-off already did, the format skeleton gains the subject slot it mandates, and the company-research sentences are gated on a brief actually being fenced.

Deliberately **not** touched: the step-by-step scaffolding. It is test-gated and its benefit was the one thing the audit could not verify empirically.

## 2. Sampling ownership

The renderer picked a temperature per task step and sent it to whatever model was configured. That is wrong on most of them now:

- Non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` returns **400 on every request** to Claude 4.7+, thinking or not.
- OpenAI reasoning models reject `temperature`.
- Google says to remove the parameters from Gemini 3 requests entirely, and documents that below 1.0 causes looping.
- Six of eight families publish one number per model with **no task dimension at all**, so the per-step table was tuning an axis no vendor supports.

Gemini already had a guard for this and it was dead code: it withheld the adapter's fallback only when the caller supplied nothing, but the renderer always supplied something, so every request looked like a deliberate user choice. The onboarding default is a Gemini 3 model, so new users hit the documented degradation case on their first generation.

The renderer now sends an **intent** and each adapter owns the numbers, behind a trait method beside `effort_levels`. Explicit values still win, so the per-model temperature sliders keep working. Anthropic needed no behavioural change — its fail-safe was already right, and the work was generalising it to the other four adapters.

### The correction that mattered

The first cut defaulted every adapter to sending nothing, on the theory that omitting is neutral. **It is not.** Omitting means the model applies its own default, which is 0.7–1.0. Measured against the live local Ollama on the author's machine:

```
qwen3.6:27b-q4_K_M   → temperature 1, presence_penalty 1.5, top_p 0.95
gemma4:31b-it-q4_K_M → temperature 1
```

So on a default local install the résumé surface would have run at 1.0 **with `presence_penalty 1.5`** — the exact knob that pushes a model toward new topics — partly undoing the prompt hardening in the same branch. Omission is right only where sending is refused or documented-harmful; everywhere else each adapter declares values reproducing today's behaviour. Anthropic and Ollama were reading the request directly and never consulted their own profile, which is what kept Anthropic's hardcoded `unwrap_or(0.7)` invisible.

Also fixed: the cover letter moves to the grounded profile (calling it "creative" was an argument about temperature, not about a penalty that rewards new topics in a letter asserting real achievements to an employer); inline rewrite returns to deterministic; the OpenAI-compatible adapter no longer hands OpenAI's numbers to arbitrary gateways; and the job analysis and inline rewrite now route through the resolver — both used bare literals, so the Settings "analysis" slider changed metadata extraction and not the analysis it is named for.

## Testing

Tests assert the **request body**, per adapter, per intent, including the absences — because the previous round asserted the intent string and every defect above passed a fully green suite. The intent vocabulary is generated from the shared schema, so a renamed literal breaks the build rather than silently degrading every request to `default`.

Guards were mutation-checked: the fix reverted, the test confirmed failing, the fix restored.

title: fix: stop the resume header rendering twice and repair pre-v0.134.0 link mojibake
body:
Two unrelated defects that showed up in one screenshot of the résumé preview.

## 1. The header rendered twice

The styled header showed the name and contact line, and then immediately a body section headed with the same name in ALL-CAPS, carrying the title and a second contact line.

Two independent causes, either of which reproduces it alone:

**Rust** — `parse_line` decided "this line is the candidate's name" from the raw line index. PDF extraction routinely emits a leading blank line, so the real name landed at index 1, missed the rule, matched `is_all_caps_section_heading` instead, and became a section header. That flips `seen_section` immediately, so the title and contact lines below were swallowed into a section named after the candidate while `header.name`/`header.contact` stayed empty and `apply_to_header` refilled them from the contact profile. The rule now keys on the first line **with content**; `idx == 0` is kept as its own arm so the original behaviour cannot regress.

**TypeScript** — `seedHeaderFromProfile` only recognised the document's own name line at exactly index 0. An ALL-CAPS name passes `isAllCapsSectionHeading`, so it read as a section boundary and the profile's name was inserted *above* it; a leading blank line produced the same shape one index down. The contact scan then broke on that line and spliced a second contact line in too. It now searches the header block for the line that already *is* the profile's name and overwrites that one in place.

Review caught three further defects in that change:
- `nameKey` claimed NFKD folds accented variants together. It does not — NFKD splits a composed character into base + combining mark, the mark is category `Mn`, and the `[^\p{L}\p{N}]+` collapse turned it into a **space**. `François` became `franc ois` and stopped matching `FRANCOIS`, so the fix silently didn't fire for accented names.
- An ALL-CAPS `fullName` in the profile left the reconciled line ALL-CAPS, so the contact scan re-tripped on it and produced a fresh duplicate.
- With no blank line anywhere in the document, the search could reconcile an occurrence of the name in the *body* and leave the header with no name at all.

## 2. Project links arrived as mojibake

A PDF text string (PDF 32000-1 §7.9.2.2) is UTF-16BE behind a `FE FF` BOM or PDFDocEncoded, never UTF-8. #955 added `pdf_text_string` to decode it, but could not touch text already written — so stored anchors still read as two replacement chars followed by every character interleaved with its NUL high byte, matched no project title, and left every link heaped at the end of the section.

`repair_utf16_mojibake` reverses it, anchored on the corruption's own shape: it requires the BOM marker followed by a NUL, then consumes only the `(NUL, ASCII)` pairs it can reconstruct. Two appended migrations rewrite the affected rows in `documents` and `ai_generations`, and the insert/update/import paths repair on write so restoring a pre-fix backup cannot re-inject the corruption.

Review shaped this one substantially:
- A per-row `UPDATE` error was swallowed. That does not do what it looks like: on `SQLITE_FULL`/`IOERR`/`BUSY` SQLite auto-rolls-back the enclosing transaction, so the loop continues in autocommit and the following `PRAGMA user_version` commits on its own — durably marking the migration applied with the row never repaired and never retried. Demonstrated by injecting `SQLITE_FULL` on a real WAL database. Store opens are already non-fatal in `lib.rs`, so propagating costs a session, not the app.
- The strip was document-wide, which deleted legitimate adjacent replacement characters elsewhere in a résumé and fused words on the html/rtf import paths.
- A UTF-16 anchor with non-ASCII code units became plausible garbage with its markers erased, destroying both the byte pairing that still made it recoverable and the marker a later repair would search for. Those rows are now left alone.
- The repair rewrote `documents.text` but left `keywords_json`, `indexed` and the `vectors` row pinned to the corrupt text, so the ATS score beside the corrected résumé would have stayed computed from mojibake forever. It now clears them.
- Both migrations snapshot the affected rows before rewriting.

## 3. Docs

`apps/landing` has been a real workspace for a while and appeared in none of the four Markdown directory listings. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` was the stalest: it called the desktop app `apps/tauri`, pointed at a `src/tauri-client.ts` that is a directory, and also omitted `apps/extension` and `packages/translations`. ADR-0021 is corrected for the in-place name reconciliation.

## Verification

`pnpm test` 4945 pass · `pnpm typecheck` clean · `pnpm lint:strict --max-warnings 0` clean · `pnpm check:agent-system` in sync · `cargo test --all-features` 3208 pass · `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` clean · `cargo test --test architecture` 18/18.

Every new guard was mutation-checked: the fix reverted, the test confirmed failing, the fix restored.

## Not included

The generation failure at reasoning effort `high` (repeating thinking text, flow resetting to the wizard) is diagnosed but deliberately left out — it is a separate concern and lands as a follow-up.

title: ui: explain what the job match and trust badges mean on hover
body:
Both job badges showed a verdict with no way to learn what it meant.

- **`MatchBand`** rendered the bare word `High` with **no description at all** on the Autopilot card. The jobs list did have a popover, but its copy is a disclaimer (*"not the employer's decision"*) that never said what the tier itself means.
- **`TrustBadge`** listed *which checks failed* (`"Suspicious domain"`) but never the verdict — which is the part that tells a reader whether to skip a posting or just look twice.

Now: `MatchBand` carries a plain-language description, and `TrustBadge` leads its tooltip with the level's meaning before the failed-check list.

## Why `title` and not a popover

`TrustBadge` uses a `HoverPopover`, so that was the obvious thing to reach for. It doesn't work for `MatchBand`:

- The Autopilot card renders the band **inside a `<Button>`** — a focusable trigger there is invalid button-in-button HTML.
- `PostingListItem` rows are an **aria-activedescendant listbox** — a trigger would add a tab stop per row.

Both constraints are already documented in comments at those call sites (`TrustBadge` passes `interactive={false}` for the same reasons). A native `title` is hover-capable and focusable-free, so it is safe in both, and it pairs with an sr-only suffix for screen readers.

`RowMatchScore` already owns a real popover, so it opts out with `describe={false}` and folds the tier sentence into its own copy — otherwise a browser tooltip would fire alongside it saying a shorter version of the same thing.

## Per-variant, not just per-tier

A `coverage` High is keyword overlap with **no AI scoring behind it**; a `combined` High blends meaning and keywords. One shared sentence would have to be vague enough to be true of both, which is how a tooltip stops being worth reading. A test asserts the two variants don't say the same thing.

## One latent bug

`TrustBadge`'s detail block was gated on the flag list being non-empty, so a flagged-but-reasonless assessment rendered a bare badge with nothing to explain it. Now gated on `interactive` alone — the level description always exists.

## Testing note

`match-band.test.tsx` stubs `t` to echo raw keys, so it **structurally cannot** catch a missing translation, and the key is built at runtime from tier + variant (`jobs.matchBand.desc.<variant>.<tier>`) so TypeScript can't either. Added `match-band.i18n.test.tsx` using real translations — the same rationale `trust-badge.test.tsx` already documents in its header — and extended the trust-badge suite.

I deleted two keys to check these guards aren't theater: **4 tests went red.** Restored after.

## Verification

| --- | --- |
| `pnpm --filter @ajh/desktop test` | 259 files / 2960 pass (14 new) |
| `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint:strict` | clean |
| Pre-push gate | pass |

**Not verified:** not looked at running. The `title` tooltip is the browser's own, so it has a ~1s delay and no styling — on the Autopilot card that's the only option without restructuring the row out of its `<Button>`. If the delay feels wrong there, that restructure is the follow-up.

title: feat: résumé trim panel, pdf link-anchor decode fix, and effort picker on every model surface
body:
Three related changes to the résumé/model surfaces, folded into one PR.

## 1 · `fix:` pdf link anchors arrived as mojibake

**Reported symptom:** generated résumés showed a block of links like
`[��g�i�t�h�u�b�.�c�o�m/…](https://github.com/…)`, detached from their project
titles.

A PDF *text string* (PDF 32000-1 §7.9.2.2) is not UTF-8 — it is either
PDFDocEncoded or UTF-16BE behind a `FE FF` BOM, and Typst, LaTeX and Word all
emit the UTF-16BE form for annotation `/Contents`. `extraction/pdf.rs` read it
with `from_utf8_lossy`, producing the BOM as `��` followed by every ASCII
character interleaved with its NUL high byte.

Both reported symptoms are one bug. The extractor writes those anchors into the
`\n---\n` reference block; `packages/prompts/src/generate/links` matches anchor →
project title to place each link. A mojibake anchor matches nothing, so every
link fell through to the unmatched-links path (`links.ts:1112`) and was spliced
in as its own item.

Adds `pdf_text_string()` (UTF-16BE / UTF-16LE / UTF-8-with-BOM / passthrough),
applied at all three sites sharing the shape: the `/Contents` anchor, the `/URI`,
and `validate/mod.rs`'s round-trip URL check.

⚠️ **Requires re-importing the résumé PDF** — the fix is at extraction time, so
already-extracted text stays mangled. I have not verified the placement fix
end-to-end on a real PDF; if links still land in a block after a fresh import,
that is a separate bug in the anchor→title matcher.

## 2 · `feat:` trim panel — rank the weakest lines for this posting

When the rendered preview exceeds the export market's customary length, an
advisory panel ranks the résumé's bullets by how little of *this* posting's
vocabulary each carries, weakest first, ties longest-first.

Embedding-free by design: reuses the `documents/keywords` kernel and the same
JD-derived stemmer as `score_one`, so the panel can never disagree with the match
score for the same pair. Zero model calls, works offline. Per-line embeddings
would have meant ~40 calls per résumé/job pair plus a cache table, and would
break whenever Ollama is down.

**Read-only** — it never edits the document; the user cuts in the editor beside it.

Adds `LocaleProfile::max_pages`, the market's customary page *count* — distinct
from `page_size`, the physical sheet on the same struct. These are hiring
conventions with no published standard (anglophone + FR/NL 2, DACH + generic-EU
3), documented as such on the field.

## 3 · `ui:` effort picker wherever a model is selected

The reasoning-effort picker only appeared in the three Settings provider
sections. `ModelSelector` is the one shared component behind all ~14 model-picking
surfaces and already computes the provider/model/baseUrl the picker needs, so
this is a single insertion there — AI Generate, Analyze, Tailor, Autopilot,
resume builder, GitHub import, interview prep, apply-by-email, referral modal and
onboarding all pick it up with no call-site changes.

Safe to render unconditionally: `EffortPicker` already returns `null` unless the
backend reports `effortLevels` for the selected model.

Moved `EffortPicker` from `features/settings/` to `components/ui/` — a shared
component importing from a feature is the wrong direction under rule 9. Added a
`compact` variant that drops the uppercase section heading (which would read as a
settings section leaking into a panel) while keeping an `aria-label` and a leading
icon.

The stored value stays **per-provider** — changing it from any surface changes it
for that provider everywhere, the same preference Settings writes.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo test --lib` | 3181 pass (11 new) |
| `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets` | clean |
| `pnpm --filter @ajh/desktop test` | 2939 pass (9 new) |
| `pnpm lint:strict` · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm gen:ipc:check` | clean |
| Pre-push gate (deny, machete, arch tests, fmt) | pass |

Notable tests: `no_market_targets_fewer_than_two_pages` pins the renderer's
skip-the-query guard, so adding a 1-page market fails a test instead of silently
hiding the panel; `utf16be_survives_accents_and_surrogate_pairs` covers the
astral-plane path a naive code-unit decode would mangle.

**Not verified:** none of this has been looked at running. The trim ranking's
*quality* on a real résumé, and the compact picker's spacing in the narrower
panels, are the two things worth eyeballing before merge.

title: fix: upload only our own debug files to sentry
body:
Found by inspecting the first real release run ([30741386889](https://github.com/saeedkolivand/ai-job-hunter-app/actions/runs/30741386889)).

## The good news first

Everything from #927/#929 worked on all four matrix legs: symbol upload `success`, flag step correctly `skipped`, assets published before symbols, no cascade into the updater jobs, `Created release 0.132.0`. **The auth token is valid** — that was the one thing tests could not prove.

## The bug

```
> Uploaded 474 missing debug information files
```

Per leg. ~1900 per release. What actually went up:

```
release/build/aws-lc-sys-.../out/chacha20_poly1305_x86_64.o
release/build/proc-macro2-.../build-script-build
release/deps/libscroll_derive-....so
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/lib/libicudata.so.70
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/lib/libudev.so.1
AI Job Hunter.AppDir/usr/bin/ajh-tauri          ← the only one that matters
```

Dependency build scripts, proc-macro `.so`s, `ring`/`aws-lc-sys` object files, and the third-party system libraries bundled into the AppImage. I had pointed `sentry-cli debug-files upload` at the whole `target/` tree.

## The fix, and why it is derived rather than guessed

Scoped to `ajh_tauri*` under `release/deps`. I took the paths **from that run's logs instead of inferring them**, which turned out to matter — my first attempt at this patch guessed `target/<triple>/release/ajh-tauri.dSYM` and would have been wrong on two platforms:

| Platform | Actual |
| --- | --- |
| Linux | `release/deps/ajh_tauri-<hash>` |
| Windows | `release\deps\ajh_tauri.exe` + **`ajh_tauri.pdb`** |
| macOS | `<triple>/release/deps/ajh_tauri-<hash>` + `.dSYM` |

On every platform the artifacts carry the **library** name (`ajh_tauri`, underscore) and sit in `deps/` — not the bin name at `release/ajh-tauri`. The guessed path would have uploaded the macOS binary **with no debug companion**: symbolication silently degraded, which is this feature's signature failure.

The copies under `release/`, `bundle/appimage/` and `bundle/deb/` are hardlinks that dedupe to the same debug id, so nothing is lost by ignoring them.

Also guarded the per-triple directory behind a non-empty check — with `matrix.target` empty the path collapses to `target//release/deps`, the same directory, enumerating everything twice.

## Verification

Simulated all three real layouts plus the empty case:

```
linux   -> 2: deps/ajh_tauri-fa4fa53a  deps/ajh_tauri-fa4fa53a.d
windows -> 2: deps/ajh_tauri.exe       deps/ajh_tauri.pdb
macos   -> 2: <triple>/deps/ajh_tauri-d8c3e74  <triple>/deps/ajh_tauri-d8c3e74.dSYM
empty   -> 0  (fails loudly, per the existing guard)
```

title: fix: keep project links out of the resume header and make them work
body:
Fixes three defects reported from one generated résumé.

## Project URLs rendered on the contact line

Project sites were swept into the contact profile's extra links at import, so the exported header rendered them on the contact line **and** again in PROJECTS. Only platform profiles may seed extra links now, and website selection prefers an apex over its own subdomains, so it no longer depends on the order links happen to appear in the source PDF.

## PROJECTS read as `Name — same-name-slug`, with no links

The prompt asked for that shape, and link injection matched the machine label literally while the PDF extractor humanised it differently — so the label never matched and nothing linked. Items now carry their real name; matching is normalised and assigns each link to its best line; job-board and non-personal profile URLs are dropped rather than becoming invented projects; and a link that still matches nothing is placed in the localized projects section or left unplaced, never appended as an orphan.

## The header in the editor differed from the exported one

Edits to it were silently discarded from PDF and DOCX while still shipping in TXT and clipboard copy. The document text now owns the header at export; the profile seeds it at generation and fills only what the text leaves blank. See [ADR-0021](docs/adr/0021-editor-owns-resume-header.md).

## Review notes

This went through three security rounds and a three-pass review ensemble before opening. Findings worth calling out, because each was invisible in the diff and only appeared when a reviewer executed the code:

- The header-seeding scan could **delete résumé content** — an entire job, a skills line, a project link — for four of the seven locales the app generates for, and for English résumés whose first heading wasn't in the recognised list. Seeding now only ever replaces one line or inserts; removal is structurally impossible.
- The Resume Builder path was never seeded, so making export fallback-only would have shipped the model's invented contact line. Both generation paths now seed through one helper, and the prompt's false promise that the line "will be replaced on export" is gone.
- A profile with only a name never seeded it, and export could not rescue it.
- The two profile lookups were unguarded and could discard a completed, already-paid-for generation.

Rules that exist in both Rust and TypeScript are now gated by shared JSON fixtures asserted from both sides, and the section-name list is read from its fixture by TypeScript rather than duplicated — after three separate bugs this session traced to a mirrored rule whose comment claimed a parity it did not have.

title: fix: warn when local ollama has no account key for company research
body:
Company research on local Ollama needs a free Ollama **account key** (credential slot `ollama-cloud`), because Ollama has no model-side web search — the app calls its web search API instead. Without the key the backend returns nothing and the renderer swallows the failure, so a missing key looked exactly like *"found nothing"*, and the cover letter was generated ungrounded with no signal to the user.

## What changed

The interview-questions modal already warned about this, and the AI-Generate fine-tune step carried its own guarded copy of the same rule. Both now consume one shared hook, and the hint appears beside the "research company" toggle in the tailor flow too. No new strings — the existing translation is reused.

## Review notes

The pre-PR review caught that the repo had **two** implementations of this predicate, and the first attempt at consolidation extracted the wrong one — dropping a cold-boot guard added by #682. Both defaults fail *into* the hint (`activeProvider` defaults to `ollama` before the config resolves, `has` defaults to `false` before the key query resolves), so an unguarded check tells a user who **already has** the key that they need to add it, on first paint of a cold session. Reproduced by executing the hook against a stub client.

The shared hook now guards both pending windows — including the key-query one, which the fine-tune copy never covered — and the fine-tune step was migrated, so there is genuinely one predicate in one place rather than two.

The hint is announced (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`): the provider picker sits directly above it, so switching providers makes it appear in response to the user's own action, and `TailorWizard` has no ambient live region the way its sibling wizards do.

Tests were tightened alongside: the a11y attributes are now asserted by role rather than text (stripping them fails the suite), and the credential-slot argument is asserted rather than discarded by the mock — previously, changing `ollama-cloud` to `ollama` would have kept every test green while pinning the hint on for every Ollama user in production.

title: feat: offer reasoning effort per model and fix embedding re-indexing
body:
Two AI-provider fixes that share the adapter files, so they ship together.

## Re-indexing reported success while writing nothing

Input was truncated to a fixed character budget that overflows a dense language's token window, every provider error was swallowed, and the batch completed regardless — so the status strip correctly read `0/1 indexed` underneath two success toasts.

Input is now chunked and mean-pooled so the whole document is embedded, the working chunk size is learned once per document and bounded, and a run that embeds nothing fails instead of reporting success. Gemini's default embedding model had been **retired by Google in January**; changing the code default fixed nothing because the resolved name is persisted, so a migration rewrites it and evicts the caches keyed on it.

## Reasoning effort reached only the Codex agent

Every HTTP adapter dropped the setting. It is now gated on the per-model reasoning capability, and the levels a picker offers come from the backend **per model** — providers publish different vocabularies per model, and an unsupported value is rejected outright.

## ⚠️ One-time effect on first launch

Stored vectors carry a format version, and this bumps it. Vectors written before this change were truncated-prefix embeddings and are **not comparable** with pooled ones, so every stored vector reads stale and lazily re-embeds. Nothing unrecoverable is deleted — only regenerable caches (`posting_vectors`, `match_scores`). This is intended and one-way.

## Review notes

A security gate plus a three-pass review ensemble ran before this opened. Findings worth calling out, because each needed the code executed rather than read:

- **The learned chunk size was poisoned by each chunk's leftover tail**, so one short remainder shrank the working size for the rest of the document. A 300,000-character résumé burned its entire call budget and failed after embedding 3% of its text. Fixed; the same document now completes in 97 calls.
- **Gemini's per-model level table was built, tested and advertised to the UI, but never consulted on the send path.** Since the setting is stored per *provider*, switching Gemini models carried a level the new model rejects straight to the API.
- **The spend ledger recorded nothing when a multi-chunk embed failed partway**, discarding calls already billed — a regression introduced by moving the paid call inside a retry loop.
- **This branch had added a model to the one-click list that Google has since shut down.** All three stale-model defects here came from hardcoded lists that were correct when written, so each such list now records the vendor page it was checked against and the date.

The adaptive embedding path moved to its own module: adding it had nearly doubled the provider module, tripping the architecture LOC rule. Split rather than allowlisted — the rule exists to report exactly that.

## The problem

Google indexes **4 of 9 pages**. Absent: `/how-it-works`, `/agent-system`, `/architecture-map`, `/world`, `/accessibility`.

Indexing tracks internal link count almost monotonically:

| Route | Inbound internal links | Indexed |
|---|---|---|
| `/download` | 7 | ✅ |
| `/privacy` | 5 | ✅ |
| `/creature` | 4 | ✅ |
| `/accessibility` | 3 | ❌ |
| `/world`, `/architecture-map`, `/agent-system` | 1 each | ❌ |
| `/how-it-works` | **0** | ❌ |

`/how-it-works` had **no `<a href="/how-it-works">` anywhere on the site**. Every other occurrence of the string is a stylesheet name, a test, a comment, or `<code>` prose. The most commercially useful page was unreachable by crawl, while a doodle short film and the privacy policy were indexed.

Compounding it, the sitemap had **never been read** — Search Console listed zero submitted or discovered sitemaps, even though `robots.ts` correctly declares it and #922 ships the file. Declaring a sitemap in `robots.txt` is evidently not sufficient. It has now been submitted manually, so the orphans will be discovered regardless; internal links still matter for crawl priority and link equity.

For context on why this matters: 3 months of traffic is **84 impressions, 2 clicks, average position 39.1**, and all 12 queries are brand-navigational. Nothing in the index answers a question anyone searches.

## Changes

- `/how-it-works` now appears in the shared footer, the homepage's own footer row, and one descriptive in-content hero link. `/agent-system` and `/architecture-map` gain footer links.
- `SoftwareApplication` JSON-LD on the homepage — the site had **no** structured data. No `aggregateRating`: there are no real reviews, and inventing one is both a Google penalty and a lie.
- Titles carry a searchable phrase; the joke moves to `openGraph.title`, which is what people actually see when a link is shared.
- The six pages that declared no `openGraph.images` now reuse the existing card.

### Titles changed — easy to veto

| Page | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `AI Job Hunter — please hire him` | `AI Job Hunter — Job Search, Résumé & Cover Letters` |
| `/how-it-works` | `— How It Works (End to End)` | `— How It Works, Step by Step` |
| `/download` | `— Download` | `— Download for macOS, Windows, Linux` |

`/creature` untouched — it is a standalone creative piece.

## Not fixed, deliberately

The 4 URLs reporting *"not indexed / Alternate page with proper canonical tag"* are `/index.html`, `/download.html`, `?ref=producthunt` and `?ref=launches.uicomet.com` — correct canonicalization working as intended, not a defect.

title: feat: make provider model listing report failures and carry model metadata
body:
PR 1 of 3 in a programme to stop hardcoding provider model lists. **No user-visible behaviour change** — this is the enabling change.

## Why

`provider-meta.ts` holds hand-curated model-id arrays. They rot silently: **four stale-model defects shipped in one session**, including a shut-down model serving as the Gemini onboarding default. Live loading already exists (`AiProvider::list_models`, all providers) and already wins at runtime — `build-options.ts` is `names = live.length > 0 ? live : m.models`, so the curated array is only a fallback.

PR 2 deletes those cloud arrays. That cannot land first, because `list_models` collapsed five distinct outcomes into `vec![]` — missing key, request failure, non-2xx, unparseable body, genuinely-empty catalogue — with `ai_list_provider_models` adding a sixth via `resolve_by_name`. Remove the fallback with that in place and every offline or erroring user gets an empty model picker and no explanation.

So the trait now returns `AppResult<Vec<Value>>`, adapters return `Err` for real failures and `Ok(vec![])` only for an empty catalogue, and the command **rejects the invoke** rather than returning an in-band error object no caller reads.

## What review found that the spec didn't

Each of these was live, and each was invisible only because the curated fallback was covering it:

| Found by | Defect |
|---|---|
| correctness | Gemini listed from `/v1` while every generation path uses `/v1beta`, so **every `-preview` model was missing** — including `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, the curated Pro-tier entry that would have silently vanished in PR 2 |
| correctness | Both cloud list endpoints paginate; only page one was read |
| correctness | A keyless OpenAI-compatible server (LM Studio, vLLM) could generate but never list |
| security | `format!("{base_url}/models")` sent requests to the **wrong path** and leaked a query-string API key into the error this PR now surfaces |

On the last one: `Url::join` is *not* the fix — a reference with no query clears the base's query, dropping the auth entirely. Resolution goes through `path_segments_mut()`, and since `reqwest::Error`'s `Display` embeds the URL and strips only userinfo, errors additionally pass through `scrub_url_secret`. `scraping/http.rs` already defends this exact class.

## Model metadata

Entries widen from `{name}` to `{name, displayName?, createdAt?, contextLength?}`. `name` is byte-identical — it is what every selection and stored preference keys on.

Every field is optional because **no field is available from every provider**, verified against each vendor's docs rather than assumed:

| | displayName | createdAt | contextLength |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | `display_name` | `created_at` | `max_input_tokens` |
| Gemini | `displayName` | **none** | `inputTokenLimit` |
| OpenAI | — | `created` (epoch) | — |
| Ollama | — | `modified_at` | — |

Gemini returns no creation date, so newest-first ordering can never be universal — which is why PR 3 keeps the onboarding default a user choice rather than a ranking rule. Absent fields are omitted, never zero-filled: a fabricated timestamp sorts wrongly and silently.

Anthropic's `capabilities` object is deliberately **not** carried — reasoning/effort gates already resolve per model via `ai_model_capabilities`, and a second provider-shaped capability source is the duplicated-rule divergence this programme keeps paying for.

## Deliberately deferred

- `base_url` arrives from the renderer on `ai_list_provider_models`; ADR-0012 says it should resolve server-side from `AiConfigStore`. Pre-existing, and fixing it properly changes several command signatures and their IPC contracts.
- Unbounded `resp.json::<Value>()` body reads — fleet-wide, belongs in `net/http.rs`.

## Verification

`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings` clean · `cargo test --lib` 3082 passed · `cargo test --test architecture` 11/11 · `pnpm gen:ipc:check` no drift · `typecheck` 13/13 · `lint:strict` clean · desktop suite 2811 passed.

Security review: **no HIGH/CRITICAL**. Correctness review: **no HIGH/CRITICAL**.

Behaviour-neutrality is covered by a new test that drives the real `ModelSelector` with a rejected query and asserts the curated fallback still renders — previously the component's `useQueries` stub made that path untestable.

title: feat: load cloud model lists from the provider instead of a curated array
body:
The payoff of the programme #935 enabled. **Deletes the hand-maintained cloud model arrays and the hardcoded onboarding defaults.**

Four stale-model defects shipped in a single session from those two places — including `gemini-2.0-flash` serving as the Gemini onboarding default after Google shut it down.

## Why both, in one PR

I originally planned these as two PRs. They aren't two concerns. They're one — **hardcoded cloud model ids that rot silently** — and splitting them ships an intermediate state that is *worse than either endpoint*: `provider-meta.test.ts` asserted that `CLOUD_DEFAULT_MODELS` pointed at a model in the curated list, so deleting the arrays alone removes that guard while leaving the hardcoded default in place, unguarded. That is precisely the hole the original bug came through.

## What replaces them

- **Last-good cache** per provider + base URL, served when a fetch fails and **disclosed as cached** rather than presented as fresh.
- **Three states that no longer look alike**: no key stored (neutral, not an error), cached list served, and a real failure showing the provider's own classified message. #935 produced those messages — 401/403 → "invalid or unauthorized API key", 429/5xx → rate limit / service error — and *nothing rendered them*. Now something does.
- **Onboarding defers the model choice** until a key exists, then the user picks from the live list. Continue blocks until they do; Skip stays always available.
- **No auto-ranked default.** Gemini's list endpoint returns no creation date at all, so a newest-first rule would silently fail for the one provider whose default actually rotted.
- Labels prefer `displayName` (`Gemini 3.6 Flash`, not `gemini-3.6-flash`); sort is stable, so a provider supplying no dates keeps its own order.
- **Keyless OpenAI-compatible can list models.** #935 allowed this in the backend for LM Studio / vLLM; the renderer gate still blocked it, so that fix was unreachable.

CLI-agent aliases (`sonnet`, `gpt-5-codex`, …) **stay hardcoded** — a local CLI binary exposes no catalogue endpoint, so they are not the same rot.

## Two regressions the deleted fallback had been hiding

**`isModelList([])` is `true`** — `every` on an empty array is vacuously true. So an empty cache entry read back as `[]`, and `if (cached)` accepted it, meaning a revoked key surfaced as *"this provider's catalogue is empty"* instead of an auth error. An operation that failed, reported as success — in the code written to make failures visible. Fixed read-side rather than write-side, so entries already written by a pre-fix build are also handled.

**An empty dropdown during load.** With the curated array gone, `options.length === 0` became reachable mid-fetch for the first time, and the branch order rendered a bare dropdown with no spinner. The test that should have caught it asserted only that the *wrong* state was absent, never that the *right* one was present — a lesson both reviewers proposed independently.

Also fixed: **Enter never configured the provider.** The onboarding wrapper's key handler took the raw `onNext`, bypassing the branch that persists the choice. Harmless when a default was auto-applied; it now discards a model the user deliberately picked. Repaired for all three modes (cloud, CLI, local Ollama).

## Accessibility

`ErrorState` and `EmptyState` in `packages/ui` had no `role`/`aria-live` — a shared-primitive fix benefiting every consumer. The new status messages are announced; focus moves to the model picker when it appears after a key save; the newly-conditional Continue explains why it's disabled instead of just dimming.

## Known, filed separately

`WelcomeStep` has the same raw-`onNext` wiring, reachable by an ordinary flow (type a name → Tab to a language tile → Enter) and it silently discards the name. Out of scope here; queued as its own fix.

## Verification

title: docs: record the no-fallback-model-list decision, and post medium review findings inline
body:
Two commits, separate concerns, both meta-level (no app code).

## 1. `docs:` — ADR-0022 + `docs/API.md`

Closes out the programme that deleted every hardcoded cloud model id (#935, #936). The decision is hard to reverse and genuinely surprising to a future reader — *"why does this app ship no model list at all?"* — so the reasoning belongs somewhere other than a diff.

Records: the four stale-model defects that prompted it; why the onboarding default is a **user choice** rather than auto-ranked (Gemini's catalogue endpoint returns no creation date, so a newest-first rule would silently fail for the one provider whose default actually rotted); why CLI-agent aliases stay hardcoded; and why the scheduled CI staleness check from the original design was **dropped** — it would have false-positived on `RATES` rows that are deliberately retained so historical spend still prices correctly.

Costs are recorded honestly too: onboarding now blocks on a network round-trip that used to be instant, and #937's regression (the keyless carve-out probing `api.openai.com` for unconfigured users) is included as the clearest illustration of what removing a fallback exposes.

`docs/API.md` gains the `listProviderModels` entry it never had, including that it now **rejects** rather than resolving an empty list.

## 2. `ci:` — inline review findings, deduped

The AI review gate could already post inline comments, but only for blocking findings (HIGH/CRITICAL at confidence ≥ 0.8). That tier almost never fires — every finding this gate has produced recently was MEDIUM or LOW, living only in the sticky comment, away from the code it describes. The capability looked absent because it almost never qualified.

**The cap was load-bearing, though.** The action's inline tool does not deduplicate across runs and this lane re-runs on every push, so an unbounded instruction stacked a fresh copy of every finding each time — noise proportional to how long a PR stays open, worst on exactly the PRs getting the most review.

So the model no longer posts at all. It writes findings; a **deterministic step** decides what gets pinned, from the same JSON the verdict already uses — the same split that keeps model prose out of the merge decision.

Dedup reuses the existing `ledgerKey`: file + category + hash of summary, **with no line number**. That omission is the point — an edit above a finding shifts its line, and a line-keyed identity would repost it as new on the next push.

A finding whose line isn't in the diff makes GitHub reject the comment, so those are skipped with a warning rather than failing the step; the sticky comment carries every finding regardless.

Lane A1 (`@claude review`) keeps its inline tool — owner-triggered, runs once, nothing to deduplicate.

### ⚠️ This PR cannot self-test the review

`claude-code-action` refuses to run when a PR edits its own workflow file (the file must match the default branch). So the **AI Review check on this PR will fail open and prove nothing** — that's the documented guard against a PR rewriting its own reviewer, not a failure. Inline posting has to be verified on the next ordinary PR after this merges.

## Verification

`pnpm gen:workflows:check` in sync · `pnpm lint:strict` clean · `scripts/ci-review-verdict.test.mjs` 10 passed (4 existing + 6 new).

The tier rule and the key's line-independence are unit-tested, since neither is observable from workflow YAML.

title: fix: stop probing api.openai.com for users who never configured it
body:
**Privacy regression introduced by #936 and currently on `main`.** Found by the post-merge review on #936.

## What happens today

#936 added a keyless carve-out so LM Studio / vLLM users could list models without storing a key:

```ts
const canFetchModels = (p: AiProvider): boolean =>
  (connected.get(p) ?? false) || p === 'openai-compatible';
```

It requires only that the provider *be* `openai-compatible` — not that it be pointed anywhere.

- `baseUrlFor('openai-compatible')` is `undefined` for anyone who never configured it.
- `OpenAiClient::new` falls back to `DEFAULT_BASE = "https://api.openai.com/v1"` on a blank base URL (`openai.rs:463-465`), sending no `Authorization` header.
- `ModelSelector` mounts on six surfaces: `ResumeBuilderPage`, `TailorFlow/StepModel`, `ReferralModal`, `JobAdView`, `AnalyzeLeftPanel`, `ai-generate/LeftPanel`.

So **every user — including a fully local, offline-by-choice Ollama user who has never touched this provider — makes an outbound HTTPS request to `api.openai.com` on every relevant page load.** For an app whose entire posture is local-first, that is the specific thing it promises not to do.

Before #936 the gate was `connected.get(p) ?? false` for every provider, so nothing fired until the user had stored something.

## Fix

`openai-compatible` fetches only once it has actually been configured — a stored base URL **or** a stored key. Every other provider keeps its stored-key gate unchanged.

Expressed as a single `isProviderConfigured(provider, connected, baseUrl)` predicate rather than a boolean special-cased per site, because the carve-out lived at **three** call sites:

- `ModelSelector/index.tsx` — `canFetchModels`
- `AISettingsTab/useProviderKeys.ts` — `expandedCanFetchModels`
- `CloudProviderConfig/index.tsx` — `canPickModel`

A change reaching some siblings and not all has produced this programme's last four defects, so the predicate exists once and the exhaustiveness was verified by grep rather than assumed.

## Preserved

- A **configured keyless** server (base URL set, no key) still lists models — the case #936 existed to enable. Covered by a test.
- A user with a key but no base URL keeps today's behaviour (resolves to the default base with their key). That predates #936 and is untouched.

## Note on the tests

**Five existing tests asserted the buggy behaviour** — fetching with nothing configured — so they were written to match the bug and would have preserved it. They now cover the configured-keyless case they were meant to protect. That's why this diff touches more test files than source files.

The new regression test asserts `listProviderModels` is never called with no key and no base URL, gated on query settlement rather than a timer (a negative assertion on a `setTimeout` fails in the direction that looks like success).

## Verification

title: fix: keep the typed name when onboarding advances by keyboard
body:
Last of the onboarding steps carrying the wiring defect fixed in `AISelectionStep` (#936).

## The bug

`WelcomeStep` passed the raw `onNext` prop to `OnboardingStepWrapper`. That prop drives exactly one thing — the wrapper's global Enter-key listener — so pressing Enter bypassed `handleNext`, which is what calls `setUserName`.

The name `<Input>` stops propagation on its own Enter handler, so this only fires once focus leaves the field. The reachable path is ordinary:

**type a name → Tab to a language tile → press Enter** → onboarding advances and the name is silently discarded.

## Fix

One line: pass `handleNext` instead of `onNext`, so the keyboard path and the button path are the same path.

## The test

Drives the real sequence — type, `user.tab()` out of the input, Enter — and asserts the name is persisted *and* the step advances.

**It was verified against the unfixed component before being accepted**: reverting the one-line fix makes it fail with `expected '' to be 'Grace Hopper'`. A regression test that has never been seen to fail isn't evidence of anything.

`WelcomeStep` had no prior test file, so the style mirrors `AISelectionStep.test.tsx`'s Enter-path block and uses the real `usePreferencesStore` (reset via `resetPreferences()`) rather than mocking it.

Two supporting cases: click-Continue persists the trimmed name, and Enter with no name typed does nothing (`canAdvance` still gates the keyboard path).

## Scope

The other onboarding steps were audited during #936 — `ResearchStep`, `AdzunaKeyStep`, `ExtensionStep`, `ResumeStep`, `AppearanceStep`, `BrowserStep` and `CrashReportingStep` are each either already wired correctly or have nothing to persist before advancing. Untouched here.

title: fix: import linkedin profiles anonymously, because signing in is what breaks it
body:
Reported as *"LinkedIn import on welcome step imports resume, but in resume settings returns an error"* — while signed in to LinkedIn.

## The direction is backwards from how it reads

Both surfaces render the same `ProfileUrlImport` and call the same `profile_import_from_url`. **There is no code-level divergence.** The difference is runtime state, and **being signed in is what breaks it**:

- The importer fetches over plain `reqwest` + `scraper` — **no browser** — and needs the `ld+json` Person block LinkedIn serves only to **anonymous crawlers**.
- It built its client from `<app_data>/browser-state/linkedin/cookies.json` whenever that existed.
- Onboarding has no LinkedIn-connect step, so a fresh install fetched as a guest → public page → parsed fine. Connect LinkedIn, and the same URL returns the authenticated SPA shell → no `ld+json` → failure.

An authenticated fetch never yields a parseable profile, so the credentials bought nothing and broke the only case that worked. The profile-import GET now always fetches anonymously, **deliberately**, with the reason in a comment — "don't send the user's credentials" reads as an oversight otherwise.

Scoped to that GET. Board scraping and login keep their cookie jar; `build_authed_client`'s other caller is untouched.

## It was failing invisibly, twice

**The success toast lied.** The *import* result was error-checked; the *save* was cast to `{ id?: string }` and `notify.success` fired unconditionally. But `documents_import` returns `json!({ "error": ... })` **in-band rather than rejecting** — so a scanned PDF or failed extraction resolved, "Profile imported" appeared, and `onImported` ran with an undefined id, silently skipping the résumé write. **The bug report's own premise may never have been true.**

**The parse reported success on garbage.** It failed only when name AND experience AND skills were all empty, with `name` falling back to `og:title` — so an authwall page with a title produced a "successful" import of an empty résumé. Success now requires a real `ld+json` name, which is precisely the field an authenticated fetch withholds.

## The error advice was pointing at the cause

`isProfileAuthError` matched `login|log in|sign in|…` and replaced the backend message with *"Connect your LinkedIn account in Settings → Accounts."* That now tells the user to do the exact thing that breaks their import — and no backend string matches it any more, so it was dead as well as wrong.

**Deleted outright rather than rewritten.** Keeping a substring classifier over messages the backend owns would rebuild the two-places-encode-one-rule drift this repo keeps paying for. The backend strings were rewritten to be user-readable, so they're shown directly, and a test asserts none of them ever says "log in" again. `resumeInput.profileLoginRequired` removed from `en` + `de`.

## Logging

The path had **zero** `tracing` calls — which is why the reporter's diagnostics bundle contained nothing about their own bug (one app line, plus ~50 `chromiumoxide` warnings that are the *login window*, not the import). It now records platform, HTTP status, whether a session was attached, and the error — but **never the URL or slug**: bundles get shared, and a profile URL identifies a person.

## Found, not fixed (out of scope)

- `board_login/mod.rs` builds cookies with no `Domain=`, so reqwest stores them host-only — a cookie for `www.linkedin.com` isn't sent to `linkedin.com`, and both spellings pass `detect_platform`. Confined to the `scrape_url::try_linkedin` paste flow; the main board scraper bypasses the jar entirely.
- `use-import-with-ocr` checks only for `scanned_pdf`, so other `{ error }` shapes are swallowed with no feedback either way.

## Verification

`cargo clippy --all-features -D warnings` clean · `cargo test --lib` 3107 · `cargo test --test architecture` 11/11 · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm lint:strict` clean · desktop 250 files / 2882 tests.

New tests cover the authwall page no longer parsing, the failed save no longer reporting success, `scanned_pdf` surfacing its message, and the rate-limited / no-public-data strings reaching the user.

title: feat: add a tech radar that fails the build when an entry goes stale
body:
A public `/tech-radar` page — what this project adopts, trials, assesses and holds, with the reasoning, linked to the ADR where one genuinely covers that choice.

## The interesting problem isn't the drawing

A radar is a **curated judgement artifact** — the same shape as the hardcoded model lists this repo just spent #935/#936 deleting because they rot silently, after four stale-model defects in a single session.

Deriving it from the manifests would remove the judgement that makes a radar worth reading. So entries stay curated, and **staleness is made to fail loudly**: every entry carries a `lastReviewed` date, and `check:tech-radar` fails when an entry names a dependency no longer present in any `package.json` or `Cargo.toml`.

**Note the deliberate asymmetry** with the CI check I argued *against* for model lists two days ago. That one would have fired on `RATES` rows retained on purpose so historical spend still prices correctly. A radar entry naming a removed dependency has no such justification. Same mechanism, opposite verdict, because the underlying data has opposite semantics.

Entries that aren't dependencies at all — techniques, hosted services, and the deliberately-not-adopted — declare a `subjectKind` and are exempt. **A check that cries wolf gets ignored**, which is precisely why the model-list version was dropped.

### Verified in both directions

```
✓ check:tech-radar OK — 40 entries checked against 179 known dependency names
✗ "Tauri 2" names dependency "zzz-not-a-real-package-tauri" — not found in any
  package.json / Cargo.toml on disk. Update the entry's dependencyName…, or move
  it to ring: 'hold' with subjectKind: 'not-adopted'…, or delete the entry entirely.
```
Exit code 1 on failure, 0 restored. A staleness check nobody has seen fail is not known to work.

## Rendering — no new dependency

`apps/landing` has exactly three runtime deps (`next`, `react`, `react-dom`) and is a static export. Zalando's radar needs d3; Thoughtworks' BYOR is canvas plus a Google Sheet. A radar is polar-to-cartesian arcs and dots, so it's **hand-written inline SVG** — d3 would have cost more than it saved.

## Accessibility

An SVG of dots is invisible to a screen reader, so the full data is **always present as a text list** — the SVG is decoration over it, not the only copy. Rings are encoded by **shape as well as colour**, every blip is a focusable anchor, and the SVG is hidden below 560px in favour of the list that was already there.

The a11y gate caught a real WCAG AA contrast failure during development (`--doc-accent` at 4.46:1) plus a heading-hierarchy skip; both fixed, and `check:a11y` is now 0 violations across 13 routes.

## Content

40 entries across four quadrants named for **this project's real shape** — Renderer & UI, Rust Core & Data, Documents & Export, Build/Ship/Trust — rather than Thoughtworks' generic set, which would have left two of four nearly empty. Verified name-by-name against the manifests. Six link a real ADR.

The **Hold** entries are real, sourced decisions (XState, a dedicated vector DB, Nominatim, Codecov + SonarCloud, a WebGL-driven landing) — that's the part of any radar that reads as credible rather than promotional, and it's a public statement about the stack, so it's worth reading closely.

## Not orphaned

In `sitemap.ts`, linked from `SiteFooter` and `DocShell`, registered in `check-parity.mjs`. #934 exists because `/how-it-works` had zero inbound links and was never indexed — a brand-new route is exactly where that repeats.

title: fix: pay off three deferred correctness defects
body:
Three independent fixes, each deferred from an earlier PR's review. Every one produces a **wrong answer without producing an error**, so none would have surfaced from ordinary use.

## 1. Cached match scores ignored the embedding vector format

`MatchScoreKey` carried provider, model and `formula_version` — not the vector version. Semantic scores are computed *from* embeddings, so a format change left every cached score a valid hit against vectors that no longer mean the same thing.

**It has been safe only by coincidence.** #933's format bump happened to land alongside a `MATCH_FORMULA_VERSION` bump, and *that* field is in the key — so scores were invalidated on the formula axis, by luck rather than by anything reasoning about vectors. The `evict_..._format_v2` migration clears `posting_vectors`, not `match_scores`.

The version is now part of the key **and** the table's primary key, so a format change invalidates by construction. Adding a `DELETE` to each future migration was the alternative, and it depends on whoever writes the next migration remembering — which is exactly what this already survived once on luck.

Raised by CodeRabbit on #933, correctly about the shape and incorrectly that it was live.

> **Found, not fixed:** `posting_vectors` has no persisted version column at all — it synthesises the current one on read, so it can never self-detect staleness and still needs a hand-written eviction per bump. That's a schema change; separate PR.

## 2. Authentication depended on how the URL was spelled

`board_login` rebuilt stored cookies as `name=value; Path=…` with **no `Domain`**, added against the stored domain minus its leading dot. Per RFC 6265 that makes them host-only — discarding the leading dot, which is the very thing marking a cookie as applying to subdomains. A session captured for `.linkedin.com` then never reached `www.linkedin.com`.

Both spellings pass `detect_platform`, so the same account silently produced an authenticated or a guest fetch depending on URL form.

A stored domain with the leading dot now rebuilds with `Domain`; one without stays host-only. **Deliberately narrow** — `Domain` is only ever the cookie's own host. Widening a session credential's scope would send it to a host it was never issued for, which is worse than the bug; where the stored shape is ambiguous it stays host-only.

The safety test (never attached to an unrelated host) was confirmed load-bearing by temporarily broadening the code and watching it fail.

Found during #940's investigation, correctly left out of that PR.

## 3. Gemini's `top_p` escaped the gate `temperature` got

Google deprecates `temperature`, `top_p` and `top_k` **together** for Gemini 3.x — ignored today, documented as a future 400. `temperature` received a per-model gate during the reasoning-effort work; `top_p` was left behind in the same commit, so two halves of one API rule disagreed about the same models.

Both now run through one `gemini_omits_sampling_params` predicate, so a future model can't be gated for one parameter and not the other. **Sharing the rule is the fix, and not sharing it is how the defect was created.**

`top_p` is omitted on v3+ *even when explicit*, deliberately unlike temperature's explicit-always-wins carve-out: temperature is a user dial, so an explicit value is intent worth honouring, whereas `top_p` here is set by our own anti-detection code — no user intent to preserve, nothing worth risking a 400 for. The reasoning is in the doc comments, because a reader would otherwise "correct" the asymmetry.

Verified against Google's current docs rather than inherited from the earlier review. `top_k` is never sent by this adapter, so it needs no gate today.

Raised on #933's review and deferred.

title: fix: bound every http body read, validate probe base urls, and stop reporting failed imports as success
body:
Four deferred items from the queue, in one branch, plus the findings from a security pass over the batch itself.

## What was wrong

**Unbounded body reads, fleet-wide.** `read_text_capped` existed but lived in `scraping/http`, so every other subsystem read response bodies with no ceiling. Moved to `net/http` (ADR-003's centralized layer) alongside new `read_bytes_capped` / `read_json_capped`, and converted every non-streaming read: geocoding, LinkedIn profile import, the six `scrape_url` resolvers, the LinkedIn client, and 26 calls across the four AI adapters. SSE and the Ollama pull-progress loop are untouched — already incremental. Scraping's own `MAX_BYTES` / `FetchOptions::max_bytes` behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Renderer-supplied `base_url` reaching the network unvalidated.** `ai_test_provider_key`, `ai_list_provider_models` and `ai_model_capabilities` handed it straight through, while the setter path has always dropped it for non-`openai-compatible` providers and run it past `ssrf::validate_provider_base_url`. Both rules now live in `resolve_by_name`, the sole entry point for all three. The parameter stays on the IPC surface — Settings deliberately tests an *unsaved* base URL so an LM Studio endpoint can be verified before saving, and local loopback/LAN endpoints keep working.

**`posting_vectors` couldn't detect a stale format.** The read synthesised `version: EMBEDDING_VECTOR_VERSION`, so `EmbeddingConfig::matches` was structurally incapable of rejecting a row. Freshness rested on a hand-maintained invariant: every future format bump had to remember its own eviction migration. Now persisted, same lesson `upsert_vector_with_conn` already carries a few lines below.

**A failed document import reported success.** `documents_import` returns errors in-band, and `use-import-with-ocr` handed every non-`scanned_pdf` error back untouched. Settings and onboarding toasted "Uploaded"; both `ResumeInputCard` paths guarded on `result.id` with no else, so failure produced no feedback at all. All four call sites already wrap `importFile` in a try/catch, so the hook throws — one change, four sites. Same shape as the LinkedIn import bug in #940.

## What the security review changed

`tauri-security-reviewer` approved with no HIGH/CRITICAL, but three MEDIUMs were worth acting on and one falsified a claim in this PR's own commit message:

- **The cap didn't cap.** The LinkedIn client disables reqwest decompression and gunzips by hand, so bounding the read bounded only the *compressed* bytes — 8 MB in, up to ~8 GB resident. Both decode sites now bound the decompressed side too.
- **`resolve_by_name` wasn't the single entry point.** `ai_set_embedding_config` persisted a `base_url` unvalidated, and it reaches egress via `embed_text` carrying the provider key and résumé text.
- **The sweep missed a read** in a file it had already converted — a discarded `.text()` on an error branch.

Plus: `read_json_capped` rebuilt on `from_slice` so it stops charset-sniffing (JSON is UTF-8 per RFC 8259; a gateway mislabelling it as `iso-8859-1` was turning valid bodies into schema errors), its parse-failure log now emits position rather than serde's message, and the `.await??` rewrite that had silently flipped an IPC error code from `PROVIDER` to `PARSE` is restored and pinned by a test.

Two test fixes worth naming: the cap test drove one oversized chunk, so it passed identically against a per-chunk guard — now three small chunks through the shared accumulator, verified by temporarily breaking the guard. And the migration idempotency test rolls `user_version` back, because `run_migrations` skips on `current >= version`, so the guard it claimed to re-exercise never ran twice.

## Also here

The macOS `xattr` command was already on the download page with a copy button, but nothing said the code block goes into the Terminal app.

`ResumeStep` took the new document id from the pre-import cached list rather than the import result, so it could record the wrong default document — or none at all on a first-ever import.

## Migration note

`add_version_to_posting_vectors` is appended at the **end** of the array. Migrations are position-indexed via `PRAGMA user_version`, so inserting mid-array would make every already-migrated install skip it forever. It defaults to `2`, not `0` — every surviving row post-dates the v1→v2 eviction wipe and is provably current, so defaulting to 0 would have re-embedded the whole posting cache for no correctness gain. The literal must not track future bumps.

## Verification

`cargo fmt --all --check` clean · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` 0 warnings · `cargo test --lib` 3133 passed · `cargo test --test architecture` 11/11 · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm lint:strict` clean · `pnpm gen:ipc:check` no drift · `pnpm test` 4864 passed.

Not in scope, flagged by the review as advisory: `read_json_capped`'s call sites all deserialize into `Value` today, so the position-only log is precaution rather than a fix.

title: fix: the macOS bug report — docx sizes, blocked pdf downloads, empty generations, and logs you can actually read
body:
From one macOS report: a CV and cover letter came out **empty**; after regenerating, the **PDF would not download**; the DOCX did download but was **132 pages of enormous text**.

The reporter's diagnostics bundle contained almost nothing, so all of this had to be reconstructed from source. Two investigations later, the most important finding is *why* the bundle was empty — that's fixed here too.

---

## Confirmed and fixed

### DOCX: 132 pages — not a Mac bug, and not their bug

`w:sz` is in half-points. Every font size went through `pt_to_dxa` (pt × 20 — correct for spacing, indentation and page geometry, not type). A 10.5pt body font was written as **105pt**; `name_pt: 20` became 200pt. Every DOCX export, every platform, every template, since the renderer was written.

24 call sites now use `pt_to_half_points`. **No test asserted `w:sz` anywhere** — the suite covered page size, fonts and colours, so the whole font-size dimension was unguarded. There are now exact assertions for both writers plus a ceiling guard that fails above 50pt.

### A failed export showed the user nothing at all

We spent two investigations working out what error message they saw. **They saw none.** Every export trigger was a bare `try/finally` with no `catch`, or a fire-and-forget `void fn()` — so the backend's perfectly readable "Export blocked: …" became an unhandled promise rejection and the button simply did nothing. That is very likely the literal experience behind "couldn't download it as PDF".

Three call sites now catch and show the backend's own message; two more are covered transitively, including one the audit missed. The export modal no longer closes itself on failure.

### Two whole-response eaters behind the empty documents

**`extractPlainText` deleted the entire document** when the model wrapped its answer in one code fence — verified at zero length for bare, language-tagged, and trailing-newline fences. This was already found and fixed in `github-projects.ts`, whose comment names the failure outright; the shared helper every résumé and cover letter runs through was never touched.

**`finish()` persisted a zero-content stream as a completed job.** A reasoning model that never reaches its `final` channel leaves `answer` empty while the stream itself succeeded, and every consumer read that as success. `finish_reason` was never parsed either, so "ran out of budget mid-reasoning" was indistinguishable from a clean empty stream — which is precisely why this needed two investigations.

The renderer's `awaitAiStream` now rejects on whitespace-only output as well.

### Cover-letter PDFs could be blocked with no way out

`header_url_mismatch` is the only critical check gated to PDF only. Its résumé arm was narrowed after two prior false-block regressions; the cover-letter arm still checked every link in the top band unconditionally, reasoning that no body *section* renders that early — which doesn't cover a body *link* in the opening paragraph. And a cover letter can't be linearised, so unlike the résumé path there was no remediation offered. Now narrowed the same way, confirmed by reverting the file and watching the new test fail on old code.

---

## Why the bundle was empty — the logging work

Adding log calls wasn't the problem. **The global level filter is `Warn`, and only `cover_letter::research` was raised to Info** — which is exactly why research briefs were the sole app content in their bundle. Every `Span` line in the app logs under one target, so raising `observability` covers ai, scrape, apply, autopilot, pipeline and export at once. A regression test pins the module path against the filter target so moving the file can't silently turn every span dark again.

**And no renderer log had ever reached the file.** `attachConsole` mirrors Rust logs *into* devtools — the opposite direction — so wiring it as I originally specified would have shipped a bridge that does nothing. The console methods now forward to the plugin, capturing every existing call site for free.

New logging: export command entry/exit and block (issue **codes**, never messages, which can embed a URL), stream start/end with lengths and finish reason, renderer generation and export start/done/failed.

⚠️ **End-to-end delivery is not verified.** The unit tests prove the forwarding logic against a mock, not that the IPC round-trip lands in the file. That needs a real run.

---

## Found while in there

**Absolute paths were being logged into shareable bundles** — an enforced `AGENTS.md` rule, violated at warn/error, so it was live. Swept the whole tree rather than fixing the two reported sites; new architecture rule **R15** fails on `.display()` inside a log macro, with an empty allowlist and four self-tests proving it catches the real multi-line shape.

**gpt-oss was billed at Claude Sonnet rates** — no matching `RATES` row, so it fell through to the 3.00/15.00 default.

---

## Not confirmed — stated plainly

**Why the PDF was blocked is still unproven.** The best-fitting explanation is `no_extractable_text`: extraction succeeds but returns under 20 characters, the signature of a PDF that renders correctly but whose text layer is unreadable. It fits everything — both document types, PDF only, DOCX fine (XML, no glyph layer), preview fine (a different serializer, no text layer at all). It could not be confirmed because the reporter's build had no logging on that path.

So this closes the **coverage gap** instead. Only one test round-tripped real PDF text through extraction, covering a single letter/layout/template combination; the 12-template résumé test asserted a `%PDF` header and a page count and nothing else. All 12 templates plus the Refined and Banded letter layouts now render and extract, asserting against the validator's own gate, with an Italian fixture including capital grave accents. **Proven to fail**: stripping `/ToUnicode` from a real rendered PDF's font objects drops extraction to zero characters and trips both assertions.

**What produced an empty stream in the first place is also unproven** — a whole-response fence and a reasoning-only completion both fit, and the two are separated by one observation: whether text appeared during streaming. Both are fixed regardless.

---

## Verification

`cargo fmt --all --check` clean · `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` 0 warnings · `cargo test --lib` 3152 passed · `cargo test --test architecture` 16/16 · `pnpm typecheck` 13/13 · `pnpm lint:strict` clean · `pnpm gen:ipc:check` no drift · `pnpm test` 4882 passed.

Deliberately left: `ollama.rs`'s own parser doesn't get `finish_reason` (local Ollama is unbilled and out of the reported path), and Ollama Cloud's `capabilities()` over-reports `supports_embeddings` for every model — real, separate, its own fix.
