title: fix: make clicking an OS notification open the app, on the right screen
body:
Two reports, one cause: clicking a Windows notification did nothing, and there was no way to jump from a notification to the thing it was about.

## Why it never worked

`tauri-plugin-notification`'s desktop `show()` is notify-rust fire-and-forget, and the `onAction` JS helper its docs point at for clicks resolves to `plugin:notification|register_listener` — a command the plugin registers **only on mobile**. Its desktop `invoke_handler` is exactly `notify`, `request_permission`, `is_permission_granted`.

So the renderer's subscription failed with `notification.registerListener not allowed. Command not found` on **every desktop startup**, and no banner click ever reached the app. `notifications_clicked` — which already focuses the window and opens the inbox — had no caller other than the tray. The capability was granted; the command simply doesn't exist off mobile.

That startup error had been happening the whole time. It only became visible after the renderer console bridge landed in #948, which is what surfaced this.

## The fix

Show the banner natively, per platform — only Windows is callback-based:

| Platform | Mechanism | Blocking? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Windows | `tauri-winrt-notification`'s `on_activated` | No — WinRT event handler |
| macOS / Linux | notify-rust's `wait_for_action` | **Yes** → runs on `spawn_blocking` |

Linux additionally needs a declared `default` action for a body click to be delivered at all. Both crates were already in the tree transitively and are pinned to the locked versions, so there's no duplicate copy.

## Deep-linking

The click now carries the clicked notification's **own** route, so "Autopilot X found 3 jobs" opens *that* autopilot instead of a list to search through.

This needed almost no new machinery: every notification source already attaches a route (autopilot → `/autopilot` with its id in `search`), and the bell's rows already followed it. The OS banner was the one surface that didn't. It goes through the same `resolveNotificationRoute` validation the bell uses, so an unknown backend route falls back to `/` rather than breaking navigation. A tray click carries no route and still just opens the inbox.

The dead `onOsBannerClick` seam is removed — contract, client namespace, mock and hook — which also silences the startup error.

## CI: macOS was compiling nowhere

Worth flagging on its own. Every Rust job runs on `ubuntu-latest`, and `macos-` appeared in no workflow except `release.yml` — so macOS-only code compiled **nowhere until a release was cut**. `Cargo.toml` already carries a comment about being burned by exactly this shape. Added a `cargo check` on `macos-latest` for PRs (check only, no bundling/tests, to stay cheap on the 10x-billed runner).

## Verification — read this before approving

- **Windows** — the failing path was reproduced first: the exact `registerListener` error was observed in the log file during a real `pnpm dev` run, which is what identified the cause. Compile-checked locally.
- **Linux** — compile-checked by CI (`ubuntu-latest`).
- **macOS** — compile-checked by the new job, and **not behaviourally verified** — I have no macOS machine. The API shape was read from the vendored `notify-rust` source rather than assumed, but whether a body click actually yields `NotificationResponse::Click` in our packaging is unconfirmed.
- Route navigation is unit-tested (exact target + search preserved, unknown route falls back, no-route opens the inbox instead), and the `notifications:open` wire shape is pinned against the renderer contract on the Rust side.

title: fix: map local Ollama's stop reason, and stop presuming an OpenAI embedding model
body:
Two follow-ups deferred from #948. I verified both against the code before touching anything — and the second one turned out **not** to be the defect I'd recorded.

## 1. Local Ollama never reported a stop reason

`parse_ollama_frames` set `usage` on the final sentinel but skipped `done_reason`, which rides on that **same object**. So `stream::finish` couldn't tell *"the model burned its whole output budget reasoning and never answered"* from *"the provider silently returned nothing"* — the exact ambiguity that made the empty generation in the macOS report unexplainable.

The non-streaming agent path (`parse_ollama_turn`) already read the field. Rather than copy the mapping, it's extracted to `ollama_done_reason` and shared — a second hand-written copy is the duplicated-heuristic defect this repo keeps re-learning. Callers keep their own precedence on top (a turn still lets `Length` outrank a tool call, since truncated tool-call JSON is worse than a truncated answer).

Also corrected the `stop_reason` doc in `stream.rs`, which now claims one fewer unmapped provider.

## 2. `text-embedding-3-small` was offered to providers that never heard of it

This is the part that wasn't what I expected. I had this recorded as *"Ollama Cloud over-reports `supports_embeddings`"*. Tracing it, the actual defect is narrower, more concrete, and **wider in blast radius**:

`default_embedding_model()` returned `text-embedding-3-small` — an **OpenAI** model id — from `OpenAiClient`. Every OpenAI-compatible client is built on it:

- **Ollama Cloud** delegates the method straight through
- **`OpenAiCompatible`** covers LM Studio, vLLM, OpenRouter

So embedding with any of them and no explicit model posted an OpenAI model id to a gateway that doesn't host it. The model-not-found came back reading as "embeddings are broken" instead of "choose an embedding model". Now gated on `id == OpenAi`, exactly the way `supports_web_search` already is.

### Why I did *not* flip `supports_embeddings`

Despite that being how I'd recorded the task:

- The boolean is **provider-level**, not per-model — the error text says so, and Anthropic is the only `false`.
- A gateway's `/v1/embeddings` endpoint may genuinely exist, and an explicit model the user knows works must still go through.
- Making it per-model needs a model-name allowlist, which breaks the zero-code-change rule for new models — and Ollama's embedding models (`all-minilm`, `bge-m3`) don't even share a name pattern, so a heuristic would produce **false negatives that block working setups**. A false negative here is strictly worse than the current false positive.

Only the presumed *default* was ever wrong. Fixing that is what actually removes the failure.

## Also

The two embedding errors were byte-identical strings for different problems. Split them: *"No default embedding model for X — choose one in Settings"* is fixable by picking a model; *"X does not support embeddings"* is not.

## Verification

Both new test groups were proven able to fail — I removed the `stop_reason` mapping and watched `parse_ollama_frames_done_carries_the_stop_reason` fail on the assertion, then restored it.

- `done_reason: length` → `Length`; `stop` → `End` (the differential — a normal completion must not claim truncation); absent → `None` rather than an invented clean end.
- `default_embedding_model` is `Some` only for native OpenAI, and `None` for both `OpenAiCompatible` and `OllamaCloud` (the latter pinned specifically because it delegates, so the gate has to hold at the inner client).

title: feat: index documents automatically, and stop the index strip reading as a chore
body:
Reported as *"after uploading a résumé I have to go to AI settings and press the indexing button"*.

## The premise was wrong, which changed the fix

`match_resume.rs:129-141` already embeds the résumé lazily when it finds no usable vector, and caches the result. **Indexing was never required** — the Settings button is a pre-warm.

And the vector has exactly one consumer: semantic match scoring. I checked every production reader. That matters, because semantic scoring is **off by default**, so for a default-config user an indexed résumé is read by nothing at all.

So what actually cost you something was (a) a slow first match — a synchronous embed inside scoring — and (b) a status strip that read like a chore list.

## 1. Say what's true

The strip said, in amber:

> N documents need re-indexing for the active model.

Nothing *needs* it. Reworded to state that matching indexes on first use, dropped the warning styling (nothing is wrong), and added a distinct line for when auto-indexing is on.

## 2. Auto-index — opt in

New `autoIndexOnUpload` preference, and one hook mounted at the root. All three moments that create stale documents surface identically as a non-zero `documents.stale`, so a single effect covers them:

- a résumé was just imported
- the embedding provider/model changed
- either of those was left over from last session

**Backed by a new command, deliberately not the existing one.** `ai_reembed_all` re-embeds *every* document unconditionally — reusing it would re-bill a cloud embedding provider for already-indexed documents every time one new file is added. `ai_index_stale_documents` embeds only what's missing and returns a null job id when nothing is, so the common case is one cheap query and no work. Both share one job body so they can't drift in error handling, cancellation or progress reporting.

## 3. Ask during setup

New onboarding step immediately before the crash-reporting consent. Both ask "may this run on your behalf", and this one calls a provider that may bill per token, so the two spend/privacy decisions sit together instead of scattered.

**Defaults to OFF**, and the step's switch is seeded from the stored value rather than forced on. Two reasons, both deliberate:

- an existing install must never start calling a paid embedding provider because of an update
- stepping back through the wizard must not silently discard a "no" — my first draft had `stored || true`, which is unconditionally true and would have done exactly that

Leaving it off costs nothing, which is the point of part 1: matching still indexes lazily.

## Tests

The hook's tests are weighted toward **not** running, since that's where the money is:

- preference off + stale documents → never called
- nothing stale → never called
- **no embedding model configured yet** → waits instead of failing once per refetch (this is the normal first-run path — the résumé step is #2, the AI step is #3)
- repeated refetches → exactly one job, not a paid duplicate per refetch
- a failing index → no unhandled rejection, and the raw provider message never reaches the log

Plus the wizard's step-count/navigation tests updated for the new step.

## Not covered

The strip's new wording and the onboarding step have no visual verification here — worth a look in `pnpm dev` before merging, since the whole point of part 1 is how it reads.

title: fix: stop squashing the embeddings checkbox, and unnest the provider row button
body:
Three UI defects in Settings → AI. Two reported off a screenshot of the shipped UI, one surfaced by the log bridge, one found while writing the tests.

## The two embeddings toggles looked like different controls

They aren't. **One cause explains both symptoms** ("the checkbox isn't the same" and "the text is too close to it"):

The row is `flex items-center justify-between` with **no gap**, and the `<input>` had **no `shrink-0`**.

- Semantic scoring's one-line description leaves slack in the row → renders correctly.
- The longer auto-index description fills the row → the copy butts against the checkbox, **and** flexbox compresses the input below its own `h-4 w-4`.

So it's not a different checkbox — it's a squashed one. Fixed on **both** rows, so a future copy change to either can't bring it back.

This is precisely the gap I flagged when #951 merged: the copy was never looked at. I reused the semantic-scoring markup and changed the text without checking the layout still held.

## `ProviderRow` nested a `<button>` inside a `<button>`

`ProviderRow` wrapped its header in `<Button variant="unstyled" onClick={onToggleExpand}>` and nested the "test key" `<Button variant="glass">` inside it.

Beyond invalid DOM: **clicking "test key" also fired the row's expand/collapse**, and assistive tech got a nested-control tree it can't express.

React had been reporting this all along — into devtools, where nobody was looking. It only became visible once the renderer console bridge started writing to the log file:

```
[2026-08-06][09:47:56][webview][ERROR] <%s> cannot contain a nested %s. ... button <button>
  <AISettingsTab> → <ProviderRow provider="ollama-cloud"> →
    <_c variant="unstyled" onClick={onToggleExpand}> → <button>
      → <_c variant="glass" onClick={onTestKey}> → <button>
```

Converted to the `role="button"` row pattern the repo already uses — `NotificationBell` carries a comment describing this exact trade-off, so the fix was to follow the existing precedent rather than invent one. Enter/Space activation preserved.

## Found while writing the tests

The semantic-scoring checkbox had **no `aria-label`**. Added.

## On the tests

Asserted on **classes, not geometry**. jsdom reports zero width/height (a documented gotcha in this repo), so a computed-size assertion would have passed happily against the broken markup — it would have been a test that could never fail.

Both layout tests were verified to fail against the shipped version before being kept: reverting `shrink-0` and `gap-3` makes them fail, restoring makes them pass.

Gates: `pnpm test` 4907 · typecheck 13/13 · `lint:strict` clean (incl. the a11y rules, which the `role="button"` conversion has to satisfy).

## Note

The remaining copy from #951 — the stale-documents line — now reads as plain information rather than the old amber warning, but I still haven't seen it rendered. Worth a glance while reviewing this.

title: feat: add the cologne navy resume template and a shared navy letter layout
body:
Ports the supplied Cologne Navy design in as a 13th résumé template, plus a fourth cover-letter layout in matching styling.

## Three of the brief's assumptions didn't hold

Each changed the work, so they're worth reading before reviewing.

**Fonts — already done.** Carlito is already bundled (`carlito_{regular,bold,italic,bolditalic}.ttf`), and `FontFamily::Calibri` already _resolves_ to it in Typst (`letter.rs`'s `font_name`). The metric-compatible substitution the brief asks for is this repo's existing convention, so "check whether Carlito is bundled, add it if not" was satisfied before I started. No new font, no new license file.

**Letter templates are not per résumé template.** The brief says "every resume template appears to ship with a matching letter template." There are **three shared layouts** behind `LetterLayout` (Classic/Refined/Banded), chosen _independently_ of the résumé template. So this adds a **fourth shared layout**, offered to every template and inheriting whichever palette is active — a Regent user picking Navy gets Regent's burgundy, not navy. Confirmed as the intent before building.

**`base` as a per-template option conflicts with the model.** `_scale.typ` is a shared house scale with locked absolute values ("change here only, never inside individual template files"), and the only per-template knobs reaching a template are page size, accent, lang, ats, has_photo. The design's "everything is a multiple of `base`" property is preserved as ratios off `body_pt`; a real size option would be a pipeline change across all thirteen templates.

## The reference's schema doesn't exist here

The standalone `.typ` consumed its own rich schema — `basics`, `skills` groups, `projects` with `stack`/`links`, `footnotes` label/value rows. This repo has **one generic IR** every template shares (`sections[].blocks[]` of paragraph/bullet/entry).

So what's ported is the **look**, not the schema — exactly how `meridian.typ` and `throughline.typ` style identical data differently. Fields with no IR equivalent arrive as ordinary runs/bullets and are styled as such. Nothing invented, no section dropped.

## ⚠️ Deviation: letter tracking

The brief specifies 0.14em on the name and 0.18em on headings, and calls the tracking core to the design. At those values **the PDF text does not extract as words**:

```
À LVA R O   È S P O S I T O     ← the candidate's name
S U M M A R Y                    ← a section heading
```

An ATS reads that as gibberish. For a job-application tool that isn't cosmetic — and the brief itself argues elsewhere that tagged/parseable PDFs matter.

Reduced to **0.06em (name) / 0.10em (headings)** — the widest values that still extract, and inside the 0.03–0.10em band every other template here already uses. Caught by `every_template_extracts_accented_latin_content`, which **fails at the brief's values**; that's how I found it rather than by eye.

If you'd rather have the exact design tracking, the honest trade is reclassifying it out of ATS tier — say the word.

## Three stale counts fixed on the way through

All in `#[ignore]`d generators, so CI never ran them and nobody noticed:

- the cover-preview generator asserted **10** files against a **12**-entry list, so it could not be run at all without editing it first
- the showcase banner hardcoded `COLS = 12` and panicked with an out-of-bounds pixel write on a 13th cell
- both printed hardcoded counts in their "written" messages (`12 SVG`, `10`) regardless of what they actually wrote

All now derive from `canonical_template_ids()`, so adding a 14th template can't leave them stale.

## Coverage

- Renders + extracts: Cologne Navy is in `every_template_renders_a_valid_pdf` and `every_template_extracts_accented_latin_content`; the Navy letter has its own accented-Latin extraction test asserting the signature after the sign-off.
- Both preview assets regenerated (résumé + cover), 13 files each.
- The exhaustive `match` caught the DOCX letter path, which needed the new layout handling too.

Nobody has _looked_ at either template rendered. The extraction tests prove text comes out; they say nothing about whether it looks like the design. Worth opening the picker before merging.

title: docs: stop claiming zero telemetry now that crash reporting ships
body:
## Why

We shipped Sentry crash reporting in #927 (ADR-0020: desktop-only, default ON, opt-out) — which reversed a published "no telemetry" promise. The **prose** in `README.md` and `SECURITY.md` was rewritten at the time. The **summary claims** were not, so the repo has been contradicting itself since.

| Where | Said |
| --- | --- |
| `README.md:166` | "local SQLite database; **zero telemetry**" |
| `Features.tsx:175` (landing home) | "OS keychain, local SQLite, zero telemetry." |
| `branding/marketing/build.mjs` | "Zero telemetry" — sub-headline **and** a pill |

The README one is the sharpest: it sits ~70 lines below `README.md:93`, which correctly says the app sends crash reports to Sentry, on by default. One file, two opposite claims.

The marketing slide is worse than the phrase alone — that panel pairs "Zero telemetry" with **"run 100% offline"**, so the two claims reinforce each other.

## What changed

All three now say **"no analytics"** and name the **opt-out crash report**, matching the `/privacy` page and the "Crash reporting" vocabulary entry in `docs/CONTEXT.md` (which reserves "telemetry"/"analytics" for behavioural and usage events — none collected — and keeps them distinct from failure reports).

`branding/marketing/04-private-ai.png` is regenerated, since the committed PNG is the asset that actually gets published. The other three slides re-rendered **byte-identical**, so no font or renderer drift snuck in, and the result was checked visually rather than assumed.

**Deliberately left alone** — the two extension-scoped claims (`apps/extension/README.md:152`, `privacy/sections/Extension.tsx:97`). The extension is excluded from Sentry and declares `data_collection_permissions: { required: ['none'] }` to Firefox AMO, so "no telemetry" is true there and load-bearing for that filed declaration. There was no mechanical guard on this claim, which is why it drifted unnoticed. Adds **check 6** to `scripts/check-landing-drift.mjs`: a denylist for `zero/no telemetry` across `README.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `branding/` and the landing source.

- Scans by **root**, not an explicit file list, so a new marketing surface is covered the day it lands rather than only the three spots we already know about.
- Allowlists the extension privacy section, and the tech-radar Sentry entry whose rationale *narrates* the reversal instead of claiming it.
- Fails loud if a scan root moves, rather than silently voiding itself.
- **Verified non-vacuous:** reintroducing the phrase into `README.md` fails the check.

It also caught my own explanatory comment in `build.mjs` on the first run, which is a decent sign it bites.

## ADR correction

ADR-0020's Consequences section claimed two things that weren't true, both now corrected in place:

1. README, SECURITY.md, ARCHITECTURE.md and CONTEXT.md "were rewritten in the same change" — the rewrite was incomplete, and README's own bullet was one of the misses.
2. `check-parity.mjs` and `check-landing-drift.mjs` "fail the build if code and copy disagree" — neither mentioned Sentry or telemetry. `check-parity.mjs` is a copy-*preservation* gate for the Next port: it asserts phrases survive, it cannot tell a surviving phrase from a true one.

title: fix: fail the release when a configured sentry symbol upload breaks
body:
The symbol upload was `continue-on-error: true`, so a wrong token or a rejected upload would skip silently — and the first you'd know is a crash report full of unresolved addresses. That is the *same* silent-failure mode this feature was reviewed for three separate times in #927.

Now that the Sentry secrets are actually provisioned, "skip quietly" only makes sense for forks.

## Changes

- **Dropped `continue-on-error`** and added `set -euo pipefail`, so any failure past the secrets guard turns the run red.
- **Moved the step after `Upload Release Assets`.** The installers are published first, so a Sentry outage or an expired token never costs a release — but the run still fails visibly afterwards. Symbols associate by debug-id, not by upload order, so nothing is lost by uploading second.
- **Absent secrets remain a legitimate skip** (a fork, or a release cut before provisioning), now emitted as a `::warning::` annotation rather than a plain log line — so **"not configured" stays distinguishable from "configured wrong"**, which is the distinction that was collapsed before.

## Verification

Parsed the workflow and asserted the invariants rather than eyeballing them:

```
YAML parses OK
assets step index: 19 | symbols step index: 20
ORDER OK: symbols upload after assets
continue-on-error: (absent - fails loudly)
```

ADR-0020 records the trade-off under Consequences.

## Note

This makes a *configured-but-broken* pipeline loud, which is the point. It cannot make the first release pass or fail on its own — whether the pasted token value is correct is still only knowable from that first run, where Sentry's "Last access" column flips from *never used*.

title: feat: add opt-out crash reporting via sentry
body:
Adds remote crash reporting to the desktop app. Plan: `.claude/plans/polished-singing-graham.md`, decision recorded in **ADR-0020**.

**This reverses a published promise.** The privacy policy named Sentry, by name, as absent in three places, and ADR-0005 defined the local-first guarantee as "no telemetry". That was a deliberate product decision by the owner, not an oversight — the docs are rewritten here in the same PR because `check:parity` and `check:landing-drift` fail if code and copy disagree.

## Why

The app was blind in production. The panic hook wrote `crashes.log` and the diagnostics zip could export it, but both required the user to notice a failure, find the export, and file an issue by hand. React errors caught by a boundary never reached `window` at all, so they were invisible even in principle.

## Scope

Desktop app **only**. The extension keeps its AMO `data_collection_permissions: ['none']` declaration true, and the landing site keeps its no-third-party-JS origin invariant (a foreign script there could read the mission-control PAT from `localStorage`).

## The four things that make "default ON" defensible

1. **Consent gate.** Transmission requires `enabled && consentShown`, not just `enabled`. The default is on, but nothing is sent until the setup wizard has actually shown the choice. A user who never finishes onboarding never reports anything — failing closed.
2. **Redaction.** Every event is serialized, every string passed through the same `redact_token` pipeline the diagnostics bundle uses (ADR-027), then deserialized. Whole-event rather than field-by-field, because a field list is a denylist that rots as the SDK adds fields. `send_default_pii` off; `server_name` overridden (the SDK otherwise sends the machine hostname, often the owner's real name).
3. **No DSN outside release.** `build.rs` bakes it from an env var set only in the signed release job, read via `option_env!`. Local builds, contributor clones and every CI check compile to `None` and cannot transmit.
4. **Extension excluded**, as above.

## Notable implementation decisions

- **Consent is Rust-owned, not a renderer preference.** `sentry::init` must run before `tauri::Builder` because `sentry-rust-minidump` forks the crash-reporter process at startup and `panic = "abort"` leaves nothing in-process able to flush a crash. There is no WebView that early, so no `localStorage` — hence a small JSON file plus an IPC pair.
- **No CSP change.** The plugin's browser side uses a custom transport that forwards WebView events to the Rust SDK over `invoke`, so the renderer never egresses. Widening `connect-src` is rated HIGH/CRITICAL in this repo; it stays untouched.
- **`sentry` is pinned to 0.42, not 0.49.** `tauri-plugin-sentry` 0.5 (the latest) builds against 0.42; a newer `sentry` links a second, type-incompatible copy and `init(&client)` stops accepting our client.
- **No hand-rolled `window.onerror`.** The injected browser SDK already installs global handlers; a second listener would double-report. Only React 19's `onCaughtError` is wired, because boundary-caught errors never reach `window`.
- **Release profile now keeps symbols** (`debug = "line-tables-only"`, `split-debuginfo = "packed"`, `strip = "debuginfo"`) and CI uploads sidecars to Sentry — never attached to the release, since full DWARF for this dep tree is large.

## Docs rewritten

All twelve claim sites, plus ADR-0005 (eighth egress class) and new ADR-0020. Two worth calling out:

- **`Footer.tsx`** claimed *"Because there's no server-side copy, deleting locally deletes it everywhere"* — flatly false once reports exist. Replaced with the erasure path.
- **`/privacy` is the policy URL filed with both Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO.** It now states desktop collection and extension non-collection as separate sections, so a reviewer cannot read one as the other while the manifest still declares `['none']`.

## Verification

`cargo test --lib` (5 new crash_reporting tests incl. the redaction gate) · `cargo test --test architecture` · `cargo clippy --all-features` · `cargo fmt --check` · `pnpm test` 4636 passed · `pnpm typecheck` · `pnpm lint` · `check:parity` against a fresh landing build · `check:landing-drift` · pre-push gate incl. cargo-deny and cargo-machete.

Claim sweep (`rg -i "no telemetry|no analytics|phones home|No Sentry"`) returns only extension-scoped hits and historical commit data.

## Known limitations, stated not hidden

- Turning reporting off unbinds the client immediately, but the minidump supervisor is a separate process forked at launch and only stops at restart. The settings copy says so.
- **5k errors/month is a quota on errors, not users.** One crash loop can exhaust it in a day. Worth setting a client `sample_rate` and per-issue server-side rate limiting before the user base grows — noted in ADR-0020, not done here.

## Needs before this actually reports

Three repo secrets: `AJH_SENTRY_DSN`, `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_ORG`, `SENTRY_PROJECT`. Without them the build compiles inert and the symbol-upload step skips itself — nothing breaks.

Follow-up to #927. I rewrote what `/privacy` says the app collects and left **`Last updated: 30 June 2026`** untouched.

The accessibility page enforces a 12-month staleness cutoff because it *promises* annual review. Nothing mechanical ties a copy edit to a date bump, so I didn't fake a guard that would either fail spuriously after 12 quiet months or give false confidence. title: docs: consolidate 13 agent rule files into a canonical agents.md
body:
## Why

The repo maintained **13 hand-written copies of the same coding rules** — and they had already drifted:

- **`NumberField`**, a primitive named in enforced rule 5, existed in `CLAUDE.md` alone. The other twelve files taught a stale primitive set.
- **`apps/landing`**, a whole workspace with its own row in the ownership table, existed in `CLAUDE.md` alone.
- `CLAUDE.md` was ~10h ahead of the rest, and every rule change meant 13 edits with nothing enforcing the 13th.

This is the exact failure the Claude Code docs warn about: *"if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily."*

## What changed

`AGENTS.md` becomes canonical — the [Linux Foundation standard](https://agents.md/), read natively by Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf and Codex. `CLAUDE.md` imports it via the [documented `@AGENTS.md` pattern](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) and keeps only Claude-Code-specific orchestration (subagent fleet, review gates, model tiering) — none of which other tools can act on.

| File | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | canonical rules, all 16 enforced rules verbatim |
| `CLAUDE.md` | `@AGENTS.md` + Claude-only layer, 57 lines |
| `.clinerules`, `.codexrules`, `.roorules`, `.jba/guidelines.md`, `.aider/system-prompt.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` | one-line pointers |
| `.windsurfrules`, `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (4) | deleted — read `AGENTS.md` natively |

**−1,398 / +101 lines.** Combined always-loaded context is 136 lines, inside Anthropic's documented 200-line target.

Updates `lint-staged` from 17.1.0 to 17.2.0
Release notes

Sourced from lint-staged's releases.

v17.2.0

Minor Changes

  • #1823 ee156cc - The chunking of tasks based on maximum command line argument length has been re-implemented to be more precise. Now the chunking happens based on the final generated command string, instead of just the list of staged files like previously. This benefits mainly Windows platforms and function commands like:

    /** @type {import('lint-staged').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*.ts": () => "tsc", // Run "tsc" when any TS file is changed (for entire project)
};

    Where the spawned command is literally "tsc" without any extra arguments. Previously, this was still chunked when a lot of files were staged. Now, it probably won't be chunked because the length of the command is just three letters.

    Also, native JavaScript/Node.js function tasks won't be chunked at all, when previously they were run multiple times when chunked:

    /** @type {import('lint-staged').Configuration} */
export default {
  "*.js": {
    title: "Log staged JS files to console",
    task: async (files) => {
      console.log("Staged JS files:", files);
    },
  },
};

v17.1.1

Patch Changes

  • #1820 a626a9f - It's now possible to set --max-arg-length=Infinity to effectively disable chunking of tasks based on the number of staged files. The parsing and validation of the numeric CLI options --max-arg-length and --concurrency has been improved.

## What

`MissionControl.tsx` was **701 lines** mixing GitHub data loading, view-model assembly, formatters, and five page sections in one file. This is PR 1 of 4 splitting the oversized `apps/landing` components.

**Pure logic → `lib/mission-control/model.ts`**, joining the eight already-tested modules in that directory:

- `RepoData` / `BenchmarkGlobal`
- `fmtInt` / `round1` / `pctOrDash`
- `safe`, `loadAll`
- `buildModel` + `type Model` — 66 lines of pure `RepoData → Model` with zero React

`actionById` moved beside `WRITE_ACTIONS` in `write-actions.ts` where it belongs.

**Markup → components**, collapsing the repeated shapes to one definition each:

| Component | Call sites collapsed |
| --- | ---: |
| `Stat.tsx` | 15 |

| `sections/{Delivery,Work,Quality,Community}Section.tsx`, `sections/MaintainerActions.tsx` | — |
| `MissionControlSkeleton.tsx` | — |

`MissionControl.tsx` now holds state, the four effects, `confirm`/`runAction`, the three `useMemo`s and composition — **235 lines**.

## Behavior

## Verification

title: refactor: split agent-fleet into sections and pure scroll modules
body:
## What

`AgentFleet.tsx` was **830 lines**: six page sections, three scroll-driven effects, and a component defined inside the render body. PR 3 of 4 splitting the oversized `apps/landing` components.

**Pure math → `lib/agent-system/`:** `links.ts` (bezier geometry), `belt.ts` (scrub progress, `activeX` interpolation, nearest-station argmin), `reveal.ts` (count-up cubic easing, scene clamp), `clipboard.ts` (copy helper + the Enter/Space `onKeyDown` that was duplicated on both `.copy-cmd` buttons), `constants.ts`.

The hardcoded `/ 9` at three sites is now `STATION_COUNT`, derived from `STATIONS.length`. The `(max-width:780px)` breakpoint, the 160ms resize debounce, the 900ms count duration, the 1300ms copied timeout and the IO thresholds are named constants instead of bare literals.

**Effects → `hooks.ts`:** `useMapLinks`, `useBeltScrub`, `useReveal`, each keeping its own rAF ticking flag and listener teardown.

**Markup → components:** six `sections/*Section.tsx`, plus `Glyph`, `Machine`, `Divider` (6 render sites), `Station` (one component rendering both the `.belt` and `.belt-vert` DOM shapes) and `NodeButton`. Hero coords, the six divider paths, legend rows, the three team lists and the save-job prompt move to `data/agent-fleet.ts` as **additive** exports — `AgentTuple`/`AUTHORS`/`PAIRS`/`CROSS_NODES`/`ROUTES`/`STATIONS`/`BY_NAME` are untouched, and `scripts/check-agent-system.mjs` still passes.

`AgentFleet.tsx` is now **29 lines**.

## The one behavior change

**`NodeButton` is hoisted from the render body to module scope.** It previously got a fresh component identity on every render, so React unmounted and remounted it — focus and CSS transitions restarted. It now takes `{ name, roleClass, selected, onSelect, onHover }`, with the three call sites passing `selected === name`, `setSelected` and `setLitName` explicitly. Everything else in this PR is behavior-preserving.

Beyond the plan, state also follows its markup: `route` into `IntakeSection`, `selected`/`litName` into `FleetMapSection`, with `useMapLinks`/`useBeltScrub` called from the sections that own their DOM. Only `useReveal` stays at the root, since `.reveal`/`.draw` spans every section. That is why the root landed at 29 lines instead of the planned ~120, with no prop drilling.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @ajh/landing typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm --filter @ajh/landing test` — 167 tests, 21 files, all pass
- `pnpm lint:strict` — clean at `--max-warnings 0`
- `pnpm exec prettier --check` — clean
- `node scripts/check-agent-system.mjs` — in sync

**This component has no unit test**, so the audit was the gate. `frontend-reviewer` verified the two risky changes empirically rather than by reading: it mounted the tree and clicked a node to confirm `aria-expanded` flips and the detail panel updates through the new component boundary, and it mounted with a synchronous fake `IntersectionObserver` to confirm the root-level `useReveal` still activates 100% of `.reveal` nodes across all six child sections. It also hand-derived Babel's JSX whitespace collapse for every `WORK_TOGETHER_TEAMS` and `FLEET_LEGEND` segment against the original — the lost-`{' '}` class of regression that has bitten this repo before. No HIGH/CRITICAL findings.

## Follow-up

The newly-pure modules (`nearestStationIndex`, `activeStationX`, `beltProgress`, `linkPathD`, `sceneProgress`, `easeOutCubic`, `countUp`) were extracted partly to be testable but ship without tests — tests were scoped out of this batch. Cheap follow-up for `test-author`.

body:
## What

`HomeBody.tsx` (**753 lines**) and `HomeBeats.tsx` (**769**) were pure static JSX — no hooks, no handlers, no logic, no imports beyond `@/lib/site-links`. Final PR of 4 splitting the oversized `apps/landing` components.

They split **verbatim** into `components/home/sections/{PageChrome,Hero,Features,Testimonials,Finale}.tsx` and `components/home/beats/Beat{1,2,3,4}.tsx`, leaving shells of **40** and **23** lines.

**No JSX was rewritten.** The repeated markup that looks like DRY bait — the ~40 decorative `<svg className="deco">` blocks, 11 `.feat` cards, 9 `.quote` blocks, 4 identical `.npc` figures — stays literal. That was a deliberate call: see below.

## Why verbatim, and how it's verified

While planning this batch I found that **ADR-0018's description of the parity gate is stale**. It claims `pnpm check:parity` "byte-matches the legacy static-site layout per page via `scripts/diff-dom.mjs` element-by-element." It does not — `check-parity.mjs` never imports `diff-dom`, and `diff-dom.mjs` has **no callers at all**; the `src/content/*/body.html` baselines it compared against were deleted in the TSX conversion. The live gate runs three *content* checks against `out/`: signature phrases, a frozen href list, installer URLs.

So there is no structural regression gate on these pages — only text and links. That is exactly why data-ifying the markup was the wrong move here, and why the split was proven by hand instead. Against a pre-split build:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tag sequence (name + id + class, document order) | 531 | **531, byte-identical** |
| Visible text (whitespace-collapsed, scripts stripped) | 38,260 | **38,260, byte-identical** |
| Direct `<section>` children of `<main>` | 8 | **8** |

## What

Two of the three follow-ups deferred from the landing component split (#914–#917). The third (tests for the extracted pure modules) is a separate PR.

**1. `scripts/diff-dom.mjs` + `diff-dom.test.mjs` deleted.** The script compared built output element-by-element against `src/content/*/body.html` baselines. Those baselines were removed in the TSX conversion (#872/#879/#881), so it has had no input and no caller since — `check-parity.mjs` never invoked it.

ADR-0018 now records what actually replaces it: a manual before/after diff of the built `out/*.html` comparing the tag sequence (element + `id` + `class`, document order) and whitespace-collapsed visible text, **with `<script>` blocks stripped from both first**. That caveat matters — Next's per-build RSC hydration payload and random `buildId` produce spurious drift otherwise. This is the check that verified #917.

**2. `work.labels` removed.** `buildModel` computed `issuesByLabel(data.issues).slice(0, 8)` and nothing ever rendered it — true before the split too. With the field gone, `issuesByLabel` had no production caller left (only its own test), so the helper and its assertions in `metrics.test.ts` go too.

**3. Two stale provenance comments** in `HomeBody.tsx` and `CookieGag.tsx` pointed at `diff-dom.mjs` to explain why the `onclick` → `onClick` conversion was safe. They now state the deviation directly.

Net **−316 / +6**.
